topic:
Complete interventional equivalence for latent feedback SCMs with exact structural support

For arbitrary finite labeled observed set X with |X|>=2 and fixed finite latent cardinality l, consider all digraphs G on X disjoint-union L with |L|=l, no self-loops, arbitrary cycles, and structural equations V=B V+E. B_ji is nonzero if and only if j<-i is an edge of G: the graph is the exact structural support. This is an explicit changed population model, not Dai equation (2), and is not a generic or Zariski-closure interpretation. All nonzero coefficient values satisfying invertibility are included, including other algebraic cancellations. Exogenous coordinates are independent, centered, nonconstant, non-Gaussian, with finite second moments and arbitrary positive variances. Fix a finite intervention family I subset of 2^X containing the empty set. Require I-B and I-B_{V\S,V\S} invertible for every S in I; no stability restriction is silently added. A perfect intervention do(X_S=x) replaces those equations by constants and preserves every other coefficient and the law of every unaffected exogenous coordinate. Population information is the tuple of full affine response kernels x -> Law(X_{X\S}^{do(X_S=x)}) for S in I, with one common B and source-law tuple across regimes. Because means are affine, these kernels are determined by residual laws at x=0 and mean responses to unit coordinate settings. The theorem is uniform over all finite sizes as input parameters; it does not assume observational irreducible reduction preserves interventions or claim to traverse unbounded latent cardinalities.

For every finite (X,l,I) and graph pair G,H on this size, define P_I(G) as the set of all tuples of response kernels produced by the model above. Derive an explicit finite graph-generated compatibility representation and prove a sound-and-complete criterion for P_I(G)=P_I(H), including cancellations compatible with exact nonzero support, intervention-invisible or merged sources, and source-law symmetries. The representation may use matching/rank information and newly derived coefficient/source compatibility relations; its exact form is a research output. Give a terminating algorithm with an explicit size-dependent complexity bound that decides equivalence and enumerates the equivalence class within the finite graph universe, modulo latent relabeling. A mere restatement as existence of B/E or black-box unrestricted quantifier elimination is insufficient: the representation and completeness proof are the hard theorem. Establish strict refinement over observational equivalence with the checked witness below, and determine exactly when independent per-regime equivalence is sufficient versus requiring additional common-mechanism invariants. Statistical theorem on the following explicit subclass only: fix N=|X|+l, finite graph family F, rational constants L>=1, kappa in (0,1/2], beta in (0,1/(8N)], and 0<s_-<s_+<infinity. Restrict every on-graph |B_ji|>=beta, ||B||_op<=L and every required (I-B_{V\S,V\S}) to minimum singular value >=kappa. Let E_i=s_i Z_i where Z_i are independent standard centered Laplace variables with density exp(-|z|)/2, and s_i in [s_-,s_+]. This is nonempty for each graph (all on-graph coefficients beta give ||B||<=N beta<=1/8 and every required minimum singular value>=7/8; use interior scales) and has E|E_i|^4<=24 s_+^4. Sample n independent observations in each of the finitely many regimes (S,x), S in I and x=0 or a unit coordinate vector in R^S; ignore regimes with no random observed coordinate. Write M for the number of retained regimes. For each output dimension k choose a fixed computable enumeration t_{k,j} of Q^k, dense in R^k and with ||t_{k,j}||<=sqrt(k)j. For two observable law tuples P,Q define d(P,Q)=(1/M) sum_v sum_{j>=1} 2^-j |phi_{P_v}(t_{k_v,j})-phi_{Q_v}(t_{k_v,j})|. This bounded characteristic-function metric separates the response-kernel tuples on the stated centered linear model. Let K_G be the compact set of law tuples under graph G and these bounds. Return a computable graph confidence superset C_n with inf_{G in F,P in K_G} P{G in C_n}>=1-alpha; and, for every fixed delta>0, uniformly over true P in the union of K_G, exclude every Gprime with inf_{Q in K_Gprime}d(P,Q)>=delta with probability tending to one. Use J_n=ceil(log2(n+1)) features per regime. Simultaneous complex characteristic-function error is at most epsilon_n=2 sqrt(log(4 M J_n/alpha)/n) by real/imaginary Hoeffding bounds; the weighted tail is at most 2^(1-J_n). A globally certified compact-parameter search, to error at most epsilon_n, computes each graph distance in these features, with explicit resolvent Lipschitz bounds proving the search terminates. No source-separation assumption is required because the rung directly compares observable characteristic functions; it makes no OICA/source-recovery or single-law exact-equivalence-class claim.

Compile each input graph/intervention family into the derived coupled structural invariant; compare invariant representations; enumerate the finite 2^((|X|+l)(|X|+l-1)) candidate digraph universe with a proved stopping/complexity bound. Enumeration may be exponential. The compiler must eliminate the unspecified source-law/structural-existence quantifier through the new representation theorem, not simply return the original feasibility question. For the statistical rung, use the specified J_n empirical characteristic-function features at the specified finite intervention settings. Model characteristic functions are explicit products of Laplace characteristic functions (1+s_i^2 u_i^2)^(-1), multiplied by the phase from the affine intervention mean. Optimize their weighted discrepancy over the compact exact-support B/scale set with edge lower margin beta to certified epsilon_n error using parameter boxes and inverse-matrix Lipschitz control. Include a graph whenever its certified lower discrepancy bound does not exceed epsilon_n; loosen this by the solver tolerance if using approximate values. Coverage follows from the simultaneous Hoeffding event. Compactness, feature tail control, and global optimization consistency prove rejection for any fixed positive d-separation. A precise finite complexity bound for the population compiler remains part of the novel theorem.

Order (L,X1,X2,X3), L latent. G equations: L=eL; X1=cL+aX2+e1; X2=bX1+e2; X3=dL+e3, where a,b,c,d are all nonzero and 1-ab!=0. Row exchange and normalization give H equations: L=eL; X1=(1/b)X2-e2/b; X2=-(c/a)L+(1/a)X1-e1/a; X3=dL+e3. Thus H redirects the latent parent from X1 to X2 while reversing the observed two-cycle. This transform is bijective on the exact nonzero-support parameters and maps independent centered nonGaussian finite-variance sources by an invertible scaled permutation, proving equality of entire observational law sets without closure or zero-pivot assumptions. Empty/singleton and all other observed-intervention systems are invertible iff the original two-cycle is. Under do(X1=z), every G kernel has Cov(X2,X3)=0, while every H kernel has Cov(X2,X3)=-(c/a)d Var(eL)!=0. Hence the interventional classes differ. The legal numeric instance a=1/2,b=1/3,c=d=1 with independent standard centered Laplace noises yields H coefficients3,2,-2; exact rational observed mixing identity holds and intervention covariance is0 versus-2 when Var(eL)=1 (or0 versus-4 for Laplace scale1). This witnesses strict refinement over observational equivalence, not yet extra refinement beyond separate intervention equivalence. Compatible statistical constants include N=4,beta=1/100,L=10,kappa=1/100,s_-=1/2,s_+=4.

Rohbeck et al., Bicycle, CLeaR 2024 (https://proceedings.mlr.press/v236/rohbeck24a/rohbeck24a.pdf), models cyclic gene regulation and evaluates unseen perturbation prediction with Frangieh et al. Perturb-seq (249 knockout targets). Its identification theory assumes no latent confounding. The result would let such perturbational analyses report the compatible hidden-variable feedback mechanisms and which predictions are common to them, rather than interpreting one fitted graph as uniquely identified. Biological application requires defending linear equilibrium semantics; no empirical performance gain is assumed.

Primary sources: Dai et al. https://arxiv.org/html/2603.04780v1; Sharifian et al. https://arxiv.org/html/2509.21423v1; Hyttinen–Eberhardt–Hoyer JMLR2012 https://jmlr.org/papers/volume13/hyttinen12a/hyttinen12a.pdf (pair condition for second-order full recovery; not joint latent graph equivalence); Taeb et al. JMLR2024 https://www.jmlr.org/papers/volume25/22-0979/22-0979.pdf (acyclic Gaussian latent intervention setting); Kocaoglu2019 https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper/2019/file/c3d96fbd5b1b45096ff04c04038fff5d-Paper.pdf and Zhou2025 https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.01037 (latent DAG I-Markov equivalence, not cyclic parametric joint-law equality). Live exact-pair and citing-followup searches through 2026-09-09 found no exact result. Internal queue/active inventory has no joint-equivalence topic. Failed/retry eid_sourcemin_cyclic_effect_rankfrontier_v1 already covers fixed-observational-law equilibrium-effect sets; it is not this graph-level multi-regime object and cannot be repackaged. Full receipts: internal/topic_selection/2026-09-09/novel_paper_sol_reads/deep_identification.md and root_checks.md. A new focused check must use the EXACT SUPPORT population convention. Prior zero-allowed witness claim is retracted and is not part of this candidate. See gate_round2_verdict.json for its counterexample; no tier is lowered to preserve it. Primary papers also checked by root: https://www.jmlr.org/papers/v13/hyttinen12a.html and https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.01037. The latter explicitly concerns indistinguishability by do-calculus invariances, not equality of full response-kernel model sets.

PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: The presolve derives an intervention pushforward identity: the observational law and affine response matrices determine every intervention residual law. Observationally invisible sources remain invisible. Diagnostic Bernoulli sources and factorization in their original support lattice yield a proposed finite source-partition criterion without restricting the population noise family. Structural realization is reduced to graph-column affine feasibility with exact nonzero coordinates, followed by independent representatives for latent columns and Hall-Rado rank inequalities. Observed columns complete the basis; principal mixing minors determine intervention solvability and response matrices. These reductions supply substantive content beyond the original coefficient-and-source existence question. The exact-support cycle-reversal witness survives all admissible coefficients, and rational checks cover feedback and hidden-source cancellation. These arguments remain unverified universal claims.
UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Complete finite comparison of the exact rank/affine charts modulo source partitions and simultaneous response equalities, including nullification and lower-dimensional strata, with an explicit size-dependent bit-operation bound. Audit every compressed step and statistical obligation listed in the draft.
EARLY KILL TEST: At N=4, compare the proposed structural-completion criterion with exact feasibility, including forced-zero coefficients, the latent two-cycle Hall failure, and degenerate affine pivot charts. A matrix passing every condition without an exact-support invertible completion refutes the compiler; repair it or pivot if full population scope cannot be preserved.

open_problems.open_problem: Does there exist an explicit finite graph-generated criterion for equality of full perfect-intervention response-kernel model sets of exact-support linear non-Gaussian SCMs with arbitrary cycles and fixed latent cardinality?

source_refs.claim: Characterizes observational distribution-set equality for linear non-Gaussian models with arbitrary latent structure and cycles using edge-rank constraints, but not coupled intervention kernels.
source_refs.author: Haoyue Dai, Immanuel Albrecht, Peter Spirtes, Kun Zhang

source_refs.claim: Characterizes latent-DAG hard-intervention equivalence through do-calculus invariances and augmented MAGs rather than equality of cyclic parametric response-kernel model sets.
source_refs.author: Zihan Zhou, Muhammad Qasim Elahi, Murat Kocaoglu

source_refs.claim: Establishes solvability conditions needed for observational and interventional distributions of cyclic SCMs to be well-defined.
source_refs.author: Stephan Bongers, Patrick Forré, Jonas Peters, Joris M. Mooij

source_refs.excerpt: graphical irreducibility without source minimality is explicitly excluded

open_problems.why_unsolved: Dai et al. reduce one observational distribution family to mixing and edge-rank data, while the prior source-minimal proposal fixes one normalized observational OICA representation and explicitly excludes joint completions and nonminimal source fibers. Perfect interventions instead expose intervention-deleted principal resolvents and affine responses that must arise from one coefficient matrix and one independent-source-law tuple. Exact nonzero support prevents replacing this compatibility problem by a generic or closure result: source splitting or merging, invisible columns, cancellations, nullification, and lower-dimensional affine charts must all remain represented. The missing proof step is a simultaneous source-partition and structural-completion theorem across every regime.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A finite combinatorial-algebraic invariant built from exact graph support, source partitions, matching/rank data, and simultaneous resolvent and affine compatibility, with an if-and-only-if equality theorem and a terminating size-bounded equivalence-class enumeration algorithm.

writing_exemplar.why: Its motivation moves from latent cyclic ambiguity to a graph-generated equivalence representation and then to complete recovery up to that equivalence.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: latent cyclic models can induce identical observational law sets -> a graph-generated equivalence object is required -> intervention families require a coupled exact-support refinement of that object

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the independent-source mixing reduction, edge-rank constraints, perfect-matching certificates, and completeness-by-graph-moves proof to simultaneous intervention-indexed principal-resolvent charts.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Both targets characterize equality of graph-indexed families of linear non-Gaussian mixtures; the new theorem adds exact support and common-mechanism compatibility across regimes.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt singular-value and algebraic-rank diagnostics with calibrated perturbation analysis to noisy estimates of the intervention-indexed rank components of the invariant.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The proposed population compiler contains latent-SEM rank restrictions, so this supplies a concrete inference route for those pieces without treating their empirical verification as automatic.

open_problems.open_problem: Exactly when does equality of the model set in every intervention regime separately imply equality of the joint multi-regime model set generated by one common coefficient matrix and one common independent-source-law tuple?

source_refs.claim: Uses pairwise twin augmented MAGs and a unified augmented representation for several hard-intervention distributions under latent DAGs.
source_refs.author: Zihan Zhou, Muhammad Qasim Elahi, Murat Kocaoglu

source_refs.claim: Uses system-wide invariances and shared SEM parameters to score a common latent-variable DAG across additive-intervention environments.
source_refs.author: Armeen Taeb, Juan L. Gamella, Christina Heinze-Deml, Peter Bühlmann

source_refs.claim: Introduces Joint Causal Inference as a shared-context SCM framework for combining observational and heterogeneous interventional data.
source_refs.author: Joris M. Mooij, Sara Magliacane, Tom Claassen

source_refs.excerpt: independent regime-wise MAG completions fail common-basal-DAG realizability
joint interventions require globally compatible assignments rather than Cartesian products

open_problems.why_unsolved: Separate regime equivalence permits a different coefficient witness, scaled source permutation, source partition, or latent completion in each regime, whereas a joint response-kernel tuple permits only witnesses that glue to one mechanism and one source-law tuple. Augmented-MAG and JCI constructions encode cross-domain graphical invariances, and Taeb et al. exploit shared parameters in an acyclic Gaussian setting, but none gives a necessary-and-sufficient lift theorem for exact-support non-Gaussian feedback models. The prior reviewer identified the same obstruction for regime-wise MAG completions. The unresolved step is to characterize when local affine/resolvent charts and source identifications form a common lift, including failures caused by nullification and inconsistent source permutations.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An if-and-only-if gluing theorem giving finite common-lift or cocycle constraints on regime-wise source partitions and affine/resolvent certificates, together with a smallest exact-support latent cyclic counterexample whenever those constraints fail.

writing_exemplar.why: Its framing makes system-wide invariance and shared global parameters the reason several perturbation datasets are more informative than separately fitted models.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: perturbation datasets share an underlying mechanism -> shared parameters impose cross-environment restrictions -> latent feedback equivalence requires a theorem deciding when separate witnesses admit one common lift

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt pairwise twin-domain comparison followed by a unified augmented object, replacing graphical-invariance equality by consistency of transition maps among coefficient and source charts.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired theorem isolates precisely the gap between separately valid regime certificates and one joint representation.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt joint likelihood scoring with shared structural parameters and environment-specific perturbation terms, proving that only globally compatible charts attain the population optimum.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It operationalizes shared-mechanism restrictions across latent-variable environments, although the destination replaces acyclic Gaussian likelihood equivalence by exact-support non-Gaussian response-kernel equality.

open_problems.open_problem: Can one construct a computable graph confidence superset with uniform finite-sample coverage and uniform exclusion of positively separated alternatives for compact exact-support latent cyclic Laplace SCMs under finitely many perfect interventions, without recovering or separating latent sources?

Every executable, effective, decision, chart-automation, and software item in this question is unresolved future work.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Graph-indexed law sets intersect, so selecting a recovered source representation or graph before inference cannot provide uniform coverage near equivalence boundaries. The earlier cyclic-effect proposal relies on recovered OICA directions and excludes loading, rank, and denominator boundaries; the BACKSHIFT proposal supplies a confidence-union analogue but leaves effective certification unresolved and uses only covariance restrictions. Direct empirical characteristic-function comparison avoids source separation, but its proof requires simultaneous finite-feature control, certified global minimization on compact exact-support parameter charts, explicit inverse-resolvent Lipschitz constants for every intervention, feature-tail control, and consistency despite intersecting graph models. Existing confidence-set and latent-SEM goodness-of-fit results do not combine these obligations.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A certified test-inversion algorithm over a finite graph family, with a nonasymptotic characteristic-function deviation theorem giving uniform coverage and a theorem uniformly rejecting every graph whose compact response-kernel family has fixed positive population distance from the truth.

writing_exemplar.why: It motivates reporting confidence sets rather than a selected graph and organizes the contribution around inversion of graph-indexed model-fit tests.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: single-graph selection hides structural uncertainty -> invert graph-indexed goodness-of-fit tests -> obtain uniformly valid graph supersets for compact latent feedback models through observable multi-regime features

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt characteristic-function continuum minimum distance and its consistency proof to graph-indexed compact intervention models, using truncated weighted features for certified computation.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Both compare explicit parametric characteristic functions with empirical characteristic functions without density estimation; the destination uses test inversion and model-set distances.

method_exemplars.technique: Carry over graph-model goodness-of-fit calibration and treatment of singular rank nulls, replacing incomplete cumulant constraints by bounded full-law characteristic-function discrepancies.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the nearest inferential treatment of latent linear non-Gaussian SEM fit and exposes why necessary moment restrictions alone cannot certify membership in the target law set.

method_exemplars.technique: Use test inversion over candidate causal structures so structural uncertainty is propagated rather than discarded after selection.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The requested output is itself a confidence superset of graphs, making graph-indexed test inversion the directly analogous proof architecture.

open_problems.open_problem: For fixed latent cardinality and an exact-support cyclic linear non-Gaussian graph universe, which families of observed-node perfect interventions are minimal or approximation-optimal for separating every pair of distinct joint interventional equivalence classes?

source_refs.claim: Represents the no-latent cyclic LiNG observational equivalence class by perfect matchings, shows how atomic interventions reveal matching information, and derives an adaptive-submodular design.
source_refs.author: Ehsan Sharifian, Saber Salehkaleybar, Negar Kiyavash

source_refs.claim: Gives necessary and sufficient experimental identifiability conditions and a complete search procedure for linear cyclic models with latent variables using interventional means and covariances.
source_refs.author: Antti Hyttinen, Frederick Eberhardt, Patrik O. Hoyer

source_refs.claim: Constructs optimal intervention families from separating systems for cyclic and causally insufficient identification settings.
source_refs.author: Antti Hyttinen, Frederick Eberhardt, Patrik O. Hoyer

open_problems.why_unsolved: The closest matching-based design argument starts from the fact that an atomic intervention exposes a matching edge, while the separating-system results target ordered-pair or simple-graph recovery. Under arbitrary latent sources and exact support, an intervention may expose only a projection of several shared source columns; merging, observational invisibility, and algebraic cancellation can prevent any unique edge or row from being revealed. Thus the first lemma supporting the existing adaptive-submodular or separating-system designs fails. Searches combining these design results with latent cyclic non-Gaussian exact-support equivalence found no design theorem whose utility is defined on the complete joint distribution-set quotient.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A characterization of separating intervention families as hitting or distinguishing sets for the coupled exact-support invariant, with a worst-case lower bound and an exact, approximation-ratio, or adaptive near-optimal intervention-selection algorithm.

writing_exemplar.why: It supplies the closest progression from observational cyclic ambiguity through a combinatorial equivalence representation to intervention selection.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: observational cyclic LiNG data leave a combinatorial equivalence class -> interventions eliminate compatible matchings -> latent exact-support classes require designs eliminating coupled source-partition and rank-compatible alternatives

method_exemplars.technique: Replace perfect-matching elimination counts by elimination counts on the coupled latent invariant, then prove adaptive submodularity or characterize its precise failure.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its design objective already acts directly on an observational equivalence class, while the destination changes the class representation and invalidates the one-edge-revelation lemma.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt separating-system and cut-cover constructions after replacing ordered-pair coverage by pairwise separation of exact-support invariant states.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It converts cyclic identifiability conditions into explicit optimal experiment families, which is the same combinatorial step required after the new equivalence criterion is available.

method_exemplars.technique: Use jointly calibrated tests of latent-SEM rank restrictions to decide which equivalence alternatives survive each selected intervention.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A finite-sample design policy must eliminate latent graph alternatives under uncertainty rather than treating population rank and matching information as known.

literature_map:
Dai, Albrecht, Spirtes, and Zhang (ICLR 2026, arXiv:2603.04780) give the closest anchor: complete observational distribution-set equivalence for latent cyclic LiNG models through edge-rank constraints and class traversal.
Zhou, Elahi, and Kocaoglu (2025, arXiv:2505.01037) characterize latent-DAG hard-intervention equivalence through do-calculus invariances and augmented MAGs, a different object from full parametric response-kernel sets.
Kocaoglu, Jaber, Shanmugam, and Bareinboim (NeurIPS 2019) provide a related latent-graph soft-intervention invariance framework.
Bongers, Forré, Peters, and Mooij (Annals of Statistics 2021, DOI:10.1214/21-AOS2064) establish cyclic-SCM solvability caveats and motivate intervention-specific invertibility conditions.
Hyttinen, Eberhardt, and Hoyer (JMLR 2012) identify linear cyclic models with latent variables from experimental means and covariances under pair and covariance conditions, but do not characterize equality of exact-support full-law sets.
Hyttinen, Eberhardt, and Hoyer (JMLR 2013) turn related cyclic identifiability conditions into separating-system experiment designs.
Mokhtarian, Salehkaleybar, Ghassami, and Kiyavash (JMLR 2023, arXiv:2205.10083) give order-optimal intervention counts for simple cyclic SCMs, without arbitrary latent-source merging or exact-support cancellations.
Sharifian, Salehkaleybar, and Kiyavash (NeurIPS 2025, arXiv:2509.21423) obtain a perfect-matching representation and adaptive-submodular intervention design for cyclic LiNG models without arbitrary latent structure.
Taeb, Gamella, Heinze-Deml, and Bühlmann (JMLR 2024, arXiv:2101.06950) exploit shared-parameter invariances under unknown additive interventions in an acyclic Gaussian latent-variable setting.
Mooij, Magliacane, and Claassen (JMLR 2020, arXiv:1611.10351) supply the multi-context shared-mechanism framework relevant to the gap between separate-regime and joint equivalence.
Schkoda and Drton (Biometrika 2025, arXiv:2311.04585) test latent LiNG moment-rank implications, but these do not yield full joint graph-set membership tests.
Wang, Kolar, and Drton (JASA 2026, arXiv:2305.14506) and Strieder et al. (UAI 2021, arXiv:2106.05694) demonstrate test inversion for causal-structure uncertainty in simpler acyclic or bivariate models.
Carrasco and Kotchoni (Econometric Theory 2017, DOI:10.1017/S0266466616000025) provide characteristic-function minimum-distance theory supporting a source-free inference route.
Rohbeck et al. (CLeaR 2024) motivate the biological destination through cyclic Perturb-seq prediction but do not establish latent-feedback graph equivalence.
Searches through 2026-09-09 located no primary result combining exact nonzero support, arbitrary latent feedback, full affine response kernels, common source laws across regimes, and a sound-and-complete finite equivalence compiler.
